q: Who is the youngest person to receive the Pritzker Prize?
n: Ryue Nishizawa was in his early forties when SANAA won in 2010. Aravena was 48 in 2016.
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates list and prize history (pritzkerprize.com)

q: Which foundation, tied to a hotel chain, sponsors the Pritzker Prize?
n: The Pritzkers owned Hyatt Hotels, and the prize is run through the Hyatt Foundation.
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates list and prize history (pritzkerprize.com)

q: The Pritzker Architecture Prize was founded in 1979 by which couple?
o: John D. and Catherine T. MacArthur
n: Jay A. Pritzker and his wife Cindy established the prize in 1979, funded through the family's Hyatt Foundation. The Pritzker family owned the Hyatt hotel chain.
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates list and prize history (pritzkerprize.com)

q: What does the Pritzker Prize recognise?
o: A living architect's built work over a career
A single outstanding building from the past year
The best unbuilt design competition entry
A lifetime of architectural writing and teaching
n: The prize honours a living architect whose built work shows a significant, consistent contribution to humanity and the built environment. No single project wins it.
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates list and prize history (pritzkerprize.com)

q: Wang Shu's 2012 prize did not name which co-founder of his Amateur Architecture Studio?
n: Lu Wenyu co-founded Amateur Architecture Studio with Wang Shu, her husband, but the prize went to him alone, as with Scott Brown and Venturi in 1991.
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates list and prize history (pritzkerprize.com)

q: The Pritzker is popularly compared to which other award?
n: The prize was modelled on the Nobel in scope and jury process, and the press routinely calls it "architecture's Nobel".
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates list and prize history (pritzkerprize.com)

q: Which firm was the first to receive the prize as a partnership of two architects?
n: Jacques Herzog and Pierre de Meuron were honoured jointly in 2001. SANAA followed in 2010, Grafton in 2020, and Lacaton & Vassal in 2021.
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates list and prize history (pritzkerprize.com)

q: Who was the second woman to receive the Pritzker Prize?
n: Kazuyo Sejima of SANAA won in 2010. Carme Pigem (2017), Farrell and McNamara (2020) and Anne Lacaton (2021) came later.
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates list and prize history (pritzkerprize.com)

q: In which year did the prize go to two architects who did not work together?
o: 2001 — Jacques Herzog and Pierre de Meuron
n: In 1988 the jury honoured Bunshaft and Niemeyer independently. 2001 and 2010 went to partnerships, and Piano and Rogers won in different years.
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates list and prize history (pritzkerprize.com)

q: Which two laureates designed the Centre Pompidou together, then won the prize in separate years?
o: Jean Nouvel and Christian de Portzamparc
n: Piano and Rogers won the 1971 Pompidou competition as partners. Piano won the prize in 1998 and Rogers in 2007. Foster and Rogers were partners too, earlier, in Team 4.
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates list and prize history (pritzkerprize.com)

q: In what year was Diébédo Francis Kéré awarded the Pritzker Prize?
n: Diébédo Francis Kéré was the 2022 laureate, remembered for the Gando Primary School in Burkina Faso (2001).
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates, 2022: Diébédo Francis Kéré

q: In what year was Christian de Portzamparc awarded the Pritzker Prize?
n: Christian de Portzamparc was the 1994 laureate, remembered for the Cité de la Musique in Paris (1995, after the 1994 prize).
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates, 1994: Christian de Portzamparc

q: In what year were RCR Arquitectes (Aranda, Pigem, Vilalta) awarded the Pritzker Prize?
n: RCR Arquitectes (Aranda, Pigem, Vilalta) were the 2017 laureate, remembered for the Les Cols Restaurant pavilion in Olot (2011).
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates, 2017: RCR Arquitectes (Aranda, Pigem, Vilalta)

q: In what year was Rem Koolhaas awarded the Pritzker Prize?
n: Rem Koolhaas was the 2000 laureate, remembered for the CCTV Headquarters in Beijing (2012, after the 2000 prize).
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates, 2000: Rem Koolhaas

q: In what year was Philip Johnson awarded the Pritzker Prize?
n: Philip Johnson was the 1979 laureate, remembered for the Glass House in New Canaan, Connecticut (1949).
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates, 1979: Philip Johnson

q: In what year was Jean Nouvel awarded the Pritzker Prize?
n: Jean Nouvel was the 2008 laureate, remembered for the Institut du Monde Arabe in Paris (1987).
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates, 2008: Jean Nouvel

q: Who received the Pritzker Prize in 2021?
n: The 2021 laureate is Anne Lacaton and Jean-Philippe Vassal. The near misses: Yvonne Farrell and Shelley McNamara won in 2020; RCR Arquitectes (Aranda, Pigem, Vilalta) won in 2017; Kazuyo Sejima and Ryue Nishizawa (SANAA) won in 2010.
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates, 2021: Anne Lacaton and Jean-Philippe Vassal

q: Who received the Pritzker Prize in 1995?
n: The 1995 laureate is Tadao Ando. The near misses: Christian de Portzamparc won in 1994; Rafael Moneo won in 1996; Fumihiko Maki won in 1993.
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates, 1995: Tadao Ando

q: In what year was Eduardo Souto de Moura awarded the Pritzker Prize?
n: Eduardo Souto de Moura was the 2011 laureate, remembered for the Braga Municipal Stadium (2003).
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates, 2011: Eduardo Souto de Moura

q: Who received the Pritzker Prize in 2009?
n: The 2009 laureate is Peter Zumthor. The near misses: Jean Nouvel won in 2008; Eduardo Souto de Moura won in 2011; Richard Rogers won in 2007.
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates, 2009: Peter Zumthor

q: Who received the Pritzker Prize in 1990?
n: The 1990 laureate is Aldo Rossi. The near misses: Robert Venturi won in 1991; Frank Gehry won in 1989; Gordon Bunshaft won in 1988.
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates, 1990: Aldo Rossi

q: Who received the Pritzker Prize in 1998?
n: The 1998 laureate is Renzo Piano. The near misses: Norman Foster won in 1999; Sverre Fehn won in 1997; Rem Koolhaas won in 2000.
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates, 1998: Renzo Piano

q: Which Pritzker Prize laureate is shown in the photo?
n: This is Gordon Bunshaft, the 1988 laureate. He is American, known for Lever House in New York and the Beinecke Rare Book Library at Yale, both with SOM. He shared the 1988 prize year with Oscar Niemeyer.
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates, 1988: Gordon Bunshaft (official portrait)

q: Which Pritzker Prize laureate is shown in the photo?
n: This is Smiljan Radić Clarke, the 2026 laureate. He is Chilean, known for the 2014 Serpentine Pavilion in London and the Teatro Regional del Biobío in Concepción.
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates, 2026: Smiljan Radić Clarke (official portrait)

q: Which Pritzker Prize laureate is shown in the photo?
n: This is Frank Gehry, the 1989 laureate. He is Canadian-born American, known for the Guggenheim Museum Bilbao and the Walt Disney Concert Hall in Los Angeles.
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates, 1989: Frank Gehry (official portrait)

q: Which Pritzker Prize laureate is shown in the photo?
n: This is David Chipperfield, the 2023 laureate. He is British, known for the restoration of the Neues Museum and the James-Simon-Galerie in Berlin.
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates, 2023: David Chipperfield (official portrait)

q: Which Pritzker-winning partnership is shown in the photo?
o: Jacques Herzog and Pierre de Meuron
n: This is Kazuyo Sejima and Ryue Nishizawa (SANAA), the 2010 laureate. They are Japanese, known for the 21st Century Museum of Contemporary Art in Kanazawa and the Rolex Learning Center at EPFL. Sejima was the second woman to win the prize.
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates, 2010: Kazuyo Sejima and Ryue Nishizawa (SANAA) (official portrait)

q: Which Pritzker Prize laureate is shown in the photo?
n: This is Gottfried Böhm, the 1986 laureate. He is German, known for the concrete Pilgrimage Church of Mary, Queen of Peace, in Neviges.
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates, 1986: Gottfried Böhm (official portrait)

q: Which Pritzker Prize laureate is shown in the photo?
n: This is Richard Meier, the 1984 laureate. He is American, known for the Getty Center in Los Angeles and the High Museum of Art in Atlanta. He was one of the "New York Five", known for all-white modernist buildings.
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates, 1984: Richard Meier (official portrait)

q: Which Pritzker Prize laureate is shown in the photo?
n: This is Zaha Hadid, the 2004 laureate. She is Iraqi-British, known for the Vitra Fire Station, MAXXI in Rome, and the London Aquatics Centre. She was the first woman to win the prize.
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates, 2004: Zaha Hadid (official portrait)

q: Which Pritzker-winning partnership is shown in the photo?
o: Jacques Herzog and Pierre de Meuron
n: This is Jacques Herzog and Pierre de Meuron, the 2001 laureate. They are Swiss, known for Tate Modern in London and the Beijing National Stadium (the "Bird's Nest").
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates, 2001: Jacques Herzog and Pierre de Meuron (official portrait)

q: Which Pritzker Prize laureate is shown in the photo?
n: This is Robert Venturi, the 1991 laureate. He is American, known for the Vanna Venturi House and the book Complexity and Contradiction in Architecture.
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates, 1991: Robert Venturi (official portrait)

q: Which Pritzker Prize laureate is shown in the photo?
n: This is Fumihiko Maki, the 1993 laureate. He is Japanese, known for the Spiral building and Hillside Terrace in Tokyo.
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates, 1993: Fumihiko Maki (official portrait)

q: Which Pritzker Prize laureate is shown in the photo?
n: This is Jørn Utzon, the 2003 laureate. He is Danish, known for the Sydney Opera House and Bagsværd Church.
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates, 2003: Jørn Utzon (official portrait)

n: The photo shows Aranya Low Cost Housing, Indore (1989), by Balkrishna Doshi, the 2018 laureate (Indian).

n: The photo shows Lloyd's Building, London (1986), by Richard Rogers, the 2007 laureate (British (born in Florence)).

q: The HSBC Main Building in Hong Kong is the work of which Pritzker laureate?
n: The HSBC Main Building in Hong Kong (1985) is by Norman Foster, the 1999 laureate, who also designed 30 St Mary Axe ("the Gherkin") in London (2004, after the 1999 prize).
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates, 1999: Norman Foster

q: The Museum of Contemporary Art in Los Angeles is the work of which Pritzker laureate?
n: The Museum of Contemporary Art in Los Angeles (1986) is by Arata Isozaki, the 2019 laureate, who also designed the Palau Sant Jordi in Barcelona (1990).
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates, 2019: Arata Isozaki

q: Which Pritzker laureate designed the Oakland Museum of California?
n: The Oakland Museum of California (1969) is by Kevin Roche, the 1982 laureate, who also designed the Ford Foundation Building in New York (1968).
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates, 1982: Kevin Roche

q: Which of these is a work of Frank Gehry?
o: The Caltrans District 7 Headquarters in Los Angeles
The Getty Center in Los Angeles
n: The Guggenheim Museum Bilbao (1997, after the 1989 prize) is by Frank Gehry, the 1989 laureate. The others: the Caltrans District 7 Headquarters in Los Angeles (2004) is by Thom Mayne; Guild House in Philadelphia (1963) is by Robert Venturi; the Getty Center in Los Angeles (1997) is by Richard Meier.
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates, 1989: Frank Gehry

q: The Hiroshima Peace Memorial Park is the work of which Pritzker laureate?
n: The Hiroshima Peace Memorial Park (1955) is by Kenzo Tange, the 1987 laureate, who also designed the Yoyogi National Gymnasium in Tokyo (1964).
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates, 1987: Kenzo Tange

q: Which of these is a work of Zaha Hadid?
o: The Perot Museum of Nature and Science in Dallas
The Vitra Fire Station in Weil am Rhein
The Marie Short House in Kempsey, New South Wales
n: The Vitra Fire Station in Weil am Rhein (1993) is by Zaha Hadid, the 2004 laureate. The others: Bagsværd Church near Copenhagen (1976) is by Jørn Utzon; the Perot Museum of Nature and Science in Dallas (2012) is by Thom Mayne; the Marie Short House in Kempsey, New South Wales (1975) is by Glenn Murcutt.
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates, 2004: Zaha Hadid

q: Which of these is a work of Rafael Moneo?
o: The Cité de la Musique in Paris
The Serralves Museum of Contemporary Art in Porto
The National Museum of Roman Art in Mérida
The San Cataldo Cemetery in Modena
n: The National Museum of Roman Art in Mérida (1986) is by Rafael Moneo, the 1996 laureate. The others: the Serralves Museum of Contemporary Art in Porto (1999) is by Álvaro Siza; the San Cataldo Cemetery in Modena (begun 1971, never fully completed) is by Aldo Rossi; the Cité de la Musique in Paris (1995) is by Christian de Portzamparc.
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates, 1996: Rafael Moneo

q: Which Pritzker laureate designed the Hotakubo Housing in Kumamoto?
n: The Hotakubo Housing in Kumamoto (1991) is by Riken Yamamoto, the 2024 laureate, who also designed The Circle at Zurich Airport (2020).
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates, 2024: Riken Yamamoto

q: Which Pritzker laureate designed the Neue Staatsgalerie in Stuttgart?
n: The Neue Staatsgalerie in Stuttgart (1984, after the 1981 prize) is by James Stirling, the 1981 laureate, who also designed the Engineering Building at the University of Leicester (1963).
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates, 1981: James Stirling

q: Which of these is a work of Hans Hollein?
o: The San Cataldo Cemetery in Modena
The Pilgrimage Church of Mary, Queen of Peace, in Neviges
The Städtisches Museum Abteiberg in Mönchengladbach
The tensile roof of the Munich Olympic Stadium
n: The Städtisches Museum Abteiberg in Mönchengladbach (1982) is by Hans Hollein, the 1985 laureate. The others: the Pilgrimage Church of Mary, Queen of Peace, in Neviges (1968) is by Gottfried Böhm; the San Cataldo Cemetery in Modena (begun 1971, never fully completed) is by Aldo Rossi; the tensile roof of the Munich Olympic Stadium (1972) is by Frei Otto.
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates, 1985: Hans Hollein

q: Which Pritzker laureate designed the Torres de Satélite in Naucalpan, Mexico?
n: The Torres de Satélite in Naucalpan, Mexico (1958) is by Luis Barragán, the 1980 laureate, who also designed Casa Barragán in Mexico City (1948).
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates, 1980: Luis Barragán

q: The Kursaal Congress Centre in San Sebastián is the work of which Pritzker laureate?
n: The Kursaal Congress Centre in San Sebastián (1999, after the 1996 prize) is by Rafael Moneo, the 1996 laureate, who also designed the National Museum of Roman Art in Mérida (1986).
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates, 1996: Rafael Moneo

q: Which of these is a work of Aldo Rossi?
o: The National Museum of Roman Art in Mérida
The San Cataldo Cemetery in Modena
The Städtisches Museum Abteiberg in Mönchengladbach
n: The San Cataldo Cemetery in Modena (begun 1971, never fully completed) is by Aldo Rossi, the 1990 laureate. The others: the Menil Collection in Houston (1987) is by Renzo Piano; the Städtisches Museum Abteiberg in Mönchengladbach (1982) is by Hans Hollein; the National Museum of Roman Art in Mérida (1986) is by Rafael Moneo.
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates, 1990: Aldo Rossi

q: Which Pritzker laureate designed the National Taichung Theater in Taiwan?
n: The National Taichung Theater in Taiwan (2016, after the 2013 prize) is by Toyo Ito, the 2013 laureate, who also designed the Sendai Mediatheque (2001).
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates, 2013: Toyo Ito
